newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical backs '97 EPS views.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical backs '97 EPS views.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp said on Thursday that its 1997 revenues would be hurt by the strong U.S. dollar, but that it still expected to meet Wall Street's earnings expectations for the company.
"We expect the dollar to have a very negative impact on our sales for the balance of the year," U.S. Surgical Chairman Leon Hirsch told a meeting of industry analysts.
"Nevertheless we are comfortable with the Street's consensus estimates on EPS."
Analysts expect U.S. Surgical to earn $1.73 a share in 1997, according to First Call. The company earned $1.48 a share in 1996.
Earlier today U.S. Surgical reported first quarter earnings of $0.39 a share which beat the consensus estimates of $0.37.
The strong U.S. dollar lowers revenues of U.S. companies by lowering the value of foreign sales in dollar terms. Hirsch
said he expected the company's gross margins to stay within a one percentage point range of the level achieved in the first quarter.
The company reported gross margins in the first quarter at 60 percent of sales.
Hirsch said U.S. Surgical planned to continue its $17 a share takeover bid of Circon Corp.
"We don't plan to drop this bid, we plan to aggressively continue," he said.
U.S. Surgical launched a bid for Circon in August but Circon has repeatedly rejected the deal, saying its board believed the offer was inadequate.
U.S. Surgical planned to file a competing proxy to nominate two directors to Circon's board of directors who would be more receptive to the U.S. Surgical bid, Hirsch said.
